ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The figure on the right is made up of six unit squares. Its perimeter is $14 \mathrm{~cm}$. Squares will be added to this figure in the same way until it is made up of 2013 unit squares (zigzag: alternating bottom right and top right). How big is the perimeter of the newly created figure?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a broken-line/zigzag chain-shaped figure composed of 6 tilted unit squares. Adjacent squares are joined along one whole side, and the whole connects alternately up and down from left to right. The problem text gives that the perimeter of this figure of 6 unit squares is 14 cm, and says to continue adding squares in the same way until there are a total of 2013 unit squares. Reasoning: According to the adding method in the figure, every time 1 unit square is added, it will share 1 complete side with the original figure. The new square originally has 4 sides, but the shared side no longer belongs to the outer perimeter, and at the same time the corresponding side on the original figure also disappears from the outer perimeter, so the net increase in perimeter is 4 - 2 = 2 cm. Originally there are 6 squares, and finally there are 2013 squares, so 2013 - 6 = 2007 squares need to be added. Therefore the new perimeter is 14 + 2 × 2007 = 14 + 4014 = 4028 cm.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the six unit squares form a zig-zag chain of tilted squares, where each square after the first is attached to the previous figure along exactly one full side. Read from the text that the 6-square figure has perimeter 14 cm and the final figure has 2013 unit squares. Use the rule that adding one unit square along one full side removes the shared side from the old perimeter and contributes the other three sides of the new square, for a net perimeter increase of 2 cm. From 6 to 2013 squares, 2007 squares are added, so compute 14 + 2(2013 - 6) = 14 + 4014 = 4028 cm.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the figure is a one-square-wide zig-zag strip with two end squares and all other squares lying between neighbors; adjacent squares share full sides, and there are no holes or branching. Generalize this same visual pattern to n unit squares. In such a chain, the two end squares each have 3 exposed sides, while each interior square has 2 exposed sides because it shares one side with the previous square and one side with the next square. Therefore the perimeter for n squares is 3 + 3 + 2(n - 2) = 2n + 2. The text asks for n = 2013, so the perimeter is 2(2013) + 2 = 4028 cm.
